objects.original: Finite sums of function sequences and their supplied component limits.
objects.reconstructed: F_i,n and G_i are E-valued functions on Omega, and the sums are finite over the whole index type I.
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; The sums range over all of the same finite index type.

domains.original: Finite measure; finite index type; seminormed additive commutative codomain.
domains.reconstructed: I finite; Omega measurable; mu finite; E a seminormed additive commutative group. F:I x N x Omega->E; G:I x Omega->E. No scalar field or vector-space structure is required.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; No scalar field is required by the SemnormedAddCommGroup binder.

quantifiers.original: For every i,n a.e. strong measurability and for each i convergence in measure imply sum convergence.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally I,Omega,E,instances,mu,F,G; assume for every i,n that F_i,n is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; assume for every i that F_i,n converges in mu-measure to G_i as n->infinity; then conclude the finite-sum convergence.
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; hF is forall i,n; h is forall i; the target has one n-limit.

assumptions.original: Exactly finite measure, finite indexing, component a.e. strong measurability and component convergence.
assumptions.reconstructed: Every F_i,n is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For each i separately, F_i,n -> G_i in mu-measure. No separate measurability assumption on G_i is written.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; hm derives measurability of finite sums; no G-measurability premise is added.

conclusion.original: Sum_i F_i,n converges in measure to sum_i G_i.
conclusion.reconstructed: The functions omega->sum_i F_i,n(omega) converge in mu-measure, as n->infinity, to omega->sum_i G_i(omega).
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; Common subsequence extraction followed by tendsto_finsetSum gives exactly the target.

scopes.original: Fixed finite family; no infinite-sum, Lp or a.s. full-sequence assertion.
scopes.reconstructed: Convergence is in measure with respect to the fixed finite mu and the seminorm-induced pseudometric. The finite index set may be empty. No L^p or almost-sure convergence is asserted.
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure.lean:12; The final step uses the in-measure subsequence criterion on finite mu.

constant_dependencies.reconstructed: No constant or rate is specified; the same finite I is fixed throughout the limit.
